sermon.title: Fair or Not Fair
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through Ezekiel 18, the “laws of life and death,” and answers the charge that “the way of the Lord is not fair.” He teaches that each person is judged by his own ways, that God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked, and that God offers a new heart, mind and spirit. He then turns to Ezekiel 33 and the watchman, and calls the church to speak what God said to speak.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: he cites “2 Timothy 4:8” for “Godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is and that which is to come”; the NKJV passage is 1 Timothy 4:8, so his words are kept and the correct passage is shown. He names several public figures and makes claims about them and about the Catholic Church and others; they appear only in the transcript, are his words, and are not verified by this site. “[Unclear]” marks five spots where the captions were not clear: two words in the reading of Ezekiel 18:14 (about 6:28–7:00) and three spots near the end of the section on Catholics (about 22:32–23:20).

chunks.section_question: What are the laws of life and death in Ezekiel 18?
chunks.short_answer: He says he is going to Ezekiel 18 and 33 to look at “the laws of life and the laws of death.” He reads Ezekiel 18:20, “the soul that sins it shall die,” and says “A law is a statement that has a punishment,” adding that “the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father.”
chunks.text:
And today we’re going to be going to Ezekiel chapters 18 and chapters 33 and we’re going to be looking at the laws of life and the laws of death. Now Ezekiel was a prophet after the first captivity. He was carried away captive about 25 years of age and uh in the in the sixth year of captivity, 31 years of age, he started prophesying. Now he’s several hundred miles away from Jeremiah who is speaking the same things. And that’s very important for you to know. These two are not connected with each other at all. Ezekiel was not even called to prophesy. Until the sixth year of the captivity.

Jeremiah had already been prophesying for quite a while. All right? And though Ezekiel is hundreds of miles away in Babylon, he is saying the same thing that Jeremiah is talking about. And it’s very important for you to know that. You see, God is a supernatural God and he does supernatural things. All right? Uh in Ezekiel 18:20 he starts out saying the soul that sins it shall die. Now that’s a law. The soul that sins it shall die. A law is a statement that has a punishment. All right? If you violate that law, there is a payment to pay.

And so the person that sins, soul is just a person that sins, it shall die. All right? Now, that’s the first thing. Number two, the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father. He says you can’t blame the son or punish the son for the father’s bad doing. Okay. Number three, nor shall the father bear the iniquity of the son. You see, my sons go out in sin and they’re of age. You know, you can’t blame me. I did my job. They just didn’t listen.

What was John the Baptist’s message? Repent. What was the apostles message on the day of Pentecost? Repent. Duh. Turn from your sins. When I say to the wicked, “You shall surely die.” All right.

chunks.section_question: What is the difference between a wise watchman and a worthless one?
chunks.short_answer: He says the wise watchman says “eternal life is by faith and keeping Bible laws, good works,” and speaks God’s laws. The worthless one says “eternal life by my faith” and lives “any way they want,” stays silent or speaks his own opinions, and does not “take personal responsibility.”

And then they live any way they want. Well, I’m saved by faith. I can just do what I want. Hallelujah. Going to heaven. Nowhere else to go. Worthless watchmen. They speak God laws. chunks.section_question: Will we be a wise church or a worthless one?
chunks.short_answer: He says “We got to make a choice to be a wise Christian or a worthless one,” and the wise one is “concerned about other people and their end result in this life and in the life to come.” He says he wants “a watchman church that is hearing from God and telling the world,” expects opposition, and says “God will prevail.”
chunks.text:
Protestants, Catholics, but somebody’s got to be a wise watchman. Can I hear an amen? Somebody’s got to decide to do it God’s way. Somebody’s got to decide to be humble, not follow the crowd, and speak what God said to speak. And that’s the way we want this church to be. We got to make a choice to be a wise Christian or a worthless one. The wise one will be concerned about other people and their end result in this life and in the life to come. You see, I don’t want to see my homosexual acquaintances die from AIDS.

It’s not just eternity. They’re dying now. They’re suffering horribly now. And all they got to do is admit they’re wrong. Ask Christ to come in and he can change that lifestyle just like he can change the drug addict, the alcoholic, the liar, the thief. So we got to decide. Are we going to be silent? Are we going to learn the word for ourselves? Are we going to not rock the boat or are we going to rock the boat so people wake up? Are we going to speak Jesus is the only way? Are we going to give in to all roads lead to the same God? That’s ridiculous. Are we going to speak up for Bible morality and withstand our adversaries?

Don’t uh diminish yourself or think lowly of yourself. God will keep adding. He knows when to add and how to add. Are you with me? The bottom line is we can be a church who is really a watchman church that is hearing from God and telling the world. And yes, we will have enemies. Yes, we will have an opponent. Yes, we will have people opposing us. But in the end, God will prevail because a people was faithful to hear his word and speak it and we will see a great harvest in America and throughout the world. Amen. So, we got to ask God this morning for that new heart and that new spirit.

faqs.question: What is a “law” according to this message?
faqs.answer: He says “A law is a statement that has a punishment.” If you violate it, “there is a payment to pay.”

faqs.question: Were Ezekiel and Jeremiah connected?
faqs.answer: He says Ezekiel was carried away captive at about 25 and began prophesying in the sixth year of captivity, “several hundred miles away from Jeremiah who is speaking the same things.” He says “These two are not connected with each other at all,” and that God “is a supernatural God.”

faqs.question: Can a father be blamed for his grown son’s sin?
faqs.answer: He says “the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father,” and “nor shall the father bear the iniquity of the son.” Of his own sons he says if they go out in sin and are of age, “you can’t blame me. I did my job. They just didn’t listen.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: The soul who sins shall die. The son shall not bear the guilt of the father, nor the father bear the guilt of the son. The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon himself, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon himself.

faqs.question: Does a person get what his own life earns?
faqs.answer: He says “If a guy does right, that he’s going to get the rewards of right. If the guy does wrong, he’s going to get the rewards of wrong.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: The soul who sins shall die. The son shall not bear the guilt of the father, nor the father bear the guilt of the son. The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon himself, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon himself.

faqs.question: Does God enjoy punishing people?
faqs.answer: He says God is “not up there saying, ‘Oh boy, I get to get that one.’” He says God asks, “Have I any pleasure delight in the wicked that they should die,” and that “He gets no delight in you dying.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Do I have any pleasure at all that the wicked should die?” says the Lord GOD, “and not that he should turn from his ways and live?

faqs.question: What good things does he say Judas did?
faqs.answer: He says Judas “followed Christ,” “preached the gospel,” “laid hands on people and they got healed,” and “cast out demons.” He says these were “right good works,” but they were forgotten when Judas betrayed Christ.

faqs.question: What does he say does not come into the equation of God’s judgment?
faqs.answer: He says God judges “Everyone according to his ways,” and that “Not grace, not faith, not the church I attend, not helping the poor, not tithing, none of those things even come into the equation.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “Therefore I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ways,” says the Lord GOD. “Repent, and turn from all your transgressions, so that iniquity will not be your ruin.

faqs.question: Are we a three-part being, according to this message?
faqs.answer: He says “you’re a three-part being … Body, soul, and spirit.” He says the soul is “the emotions, the intellect, and the will,” and that when the body dies “the spirit continues.”

faqs.question: How does he say you get a new mind?
faqs.answer: He asks, “if preachers don’t preach the word, how you going to get a new mind? If you don’t write, read, and study the word, how you going to get a new mind?”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.

faqs.question: What responsibility does he say the church has?
faqs.answer: He says “you have a responsibility. This church has a responsibility,” and that “Christianity isn’t just Disneyland.” The watchman’s job is to warn people of coming destruction.

scriptures.text_nkjv: “So you, son of man: I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel; therefore you shall hear a word from My mouth and warn them for Me. When I say to the wicked, ‘O wicked man, you shall surely die!’ and you do not speak to warn the wicked from his way, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood I will require at your hand. Nevertheless if you warn the wicked to turn from his way, and he does not turn from his way, he shall die in his iniquity; but you have delivered your soul.

faqs.question: What message was the watchman to give?
faqs.answer: He says the message to Ezekiel was “Repent,” and that it was also Jesus’s first message, “Repent and believe the gospel,” John the Baptist’s message and the apostles’ message on the day of Pentecost.

faqs.question: Is it enough to keep your faith private?
faqs.answer: He says people say “I don’t wear my Christianity on my sleeve,” and answers “you better be wearing it somewhere where people can see it.”

faqs.question: What does he say about Christianity having a place in public life?
faqs.answer: He says “America’s got us being politically correct that Christianity has no place in the public,” and asks “where does secularism have a place in the public?” He says secular means non-spiritual, and that it is “not in the constitution and it’s not in common sense.”

faqs.question: What does he say about blaming others for our actions?
faqs.answer: He lists among the marks of the worthless watchman: “Blame society. Blame your parents. … Don’t take personal responsibility for your actions.”

faqs.question: What kind of church does he want this to be?
faqs.answer: He says “we can be a church who is really a watchman church that is hearing from God and telling the world.” He says there will be opposition, “But in the end, God will prevail because a people was faithful to hear his word and speak it.”
